questions.enonce_markdown: Mr. Chukwu, a foreign businessman residing in Kumba, recently acquired Cameroonian citizenship. In which of the following ways did he achieve this?
questions.corrige_markdown:
A foreigner who settles in a country and later obtains its citizenship by following the legal procedure becomes a citizen by **naturalization**. Citizenship by birth is for people born to a citizen of the country (or, depending on the law, in its territory), so it does not apply to a foreign businessman who is already an adult. Nationalization is the transfer of private property or businesses to the State, not a way of acquiring citizenship. Territorial expansion concerns a whole population that becomes part of a country when borders change, not an individual case.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The foundation of a successful home is built on...
questions.corrige_markdown:
A successful home is a place where members live in harmony, respect one another and support one another. These qualities come from **love**, which leads to understanding, sharing, forgiveness and cooperation. Material wealth, friends and cleanliness are useful but they are not the foundation: a rich home without love can still break down, and a home with little money but with love can stay united.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Identify the type of family where husband and wife live together with their children and related members of the family.
questions.corrige_markdown:
An **extended family** includes the husband, the wife and their children together with other relatives such as grandparents, uncles, aunts and cousins. A nuclear family has only the parents and their children, so the presence of related members rules it out. A monogamous family is one with one husband and one wife, and a polygamous family has one husband with more than one wife; both words describe the marriage and not the presence of relatives in the household.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Select the letter linked to the most important natural right of a child.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Natural rights are rights a child has because he or she is a human being. The **right to life** is the most important of them because no other right (name, education, expression) can be enjoyed if the child is not alive. For this reason the right to life is the first right protected in human rights texts, including those on children's rights.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: An extensive area with people having similar language, culture and history is known as...
questions.corrige_markdown:
An **ethnic group** is a large community of people who share a common language, culture and history and who often live in the same wide area. A clan is smaller: it groups families that claim a common ancestor. A village is a small settlement, and a tribe is usually used for a smaller or more traditional unit than an ethnic group. The words "extensive area" point to the ethnic group.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: An important traffic device that controls the movement of vehicles and pedestrians in major road junctions is known as...
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Traffic lights** use red, amber (yellow) and green signals to tell drivers and pedestrians when to stop, get ready and go at busy junctions. Speed bumps only slow vehicles down, pavement markings guide road users but do not control the order of movement, and the traffic police are people and not a device.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The slogan "Avoid alcohol when driving" is intended to...
questions.corrige_markdown:
Alcohol slows reactions, weakens judgement and reduces attention, and drunk driving is a major cause of accidents. The slogan therefore aims to **combat road accidents**. It does not ask people to stop drinking in general (it only asks them not to mix drinking and driving), it does not speak about road signs, and its purpose is prevention and not to trap road users.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The PTA of a school institution can assist the school in doing all of the following except...
questions.corrige_markdown:
A Parents-Teachers Association (PTA) is made up of parents and teachers who support the school with money and materials. It commonly helps to build or repair classrooms and other infrastructure, to motivate teachers (for example with bonuses or rewards for good results) and to support school events such as prize-giving days. Organising seminars to upgrade the **professional knowledge** of teachers belongs to the educational authorities and the pedagogic bodies of the Ministry, so it is the activity that is not a normal PTA role.

**Answer: C.**

choix.texte: organising seminars to upgrade teachers' knowledge.
supporting school events such as prize awards.

questions.enonce_markdown: Which one of the following is a function of a council in Cameroon?
questions.corrige_markdown:
A council (commune) keeps the civil status registers: births, marriages and deaths are recorded and certificates are issued at the council, which makes **civil status registration** a council function. Divorce is granted by the courts, secondary schools are created by the State through the Ministry in charge of secondary education, and land titles are issued by the State services in charge of lands.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The most outstanding negative economic consequence of rural urban migration on the village is...
questions.corrige_markdown:
When young and active people leave the village for towns, the village loses the labour force that farms the land, builds and runs local activities, so production falls: this is the **loss of man power**. A low crime wave is a positive effect and not economic, unemployment is the problem of the towns that receive the migrants, and a reduction in population is a demographic effect and not specifically an economic one.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: What is the traditional value found in the act of villagers giving warm reception to visitors?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Welcoming visitors warmly, offering them food, drink and a place to rest, is the traditional value of **hospitality**. Kindness and generosity are wider qualities (being caring or giving freely) and receptiveness means being open to ideas, while hospitality is the exact word for the warm reception of guests.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following local government officials is appointed?
questions.corrige_markdown:
In Cameroon councillors are elected by voters, and the mayor and deputy mayors are elected by the councillors from among themselves. The **Secretary General** of the council, on the other hand, is an administrative official who is appointed and is not elected. The councillor, the deputy mayor and the city mayor all hold elected positions.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The greatest agent of environmental degradation is...
questions.corrige_markdown:
Industrialisation, deforestation and the other processes listed are all activities carried out by people. Human beings cut trees, burn bushes, pollute water and air and over-use natural resources, so **man** is the greatest agent of environmental degradation. Globalisation, industrialisation and deforestation are causes or forms of degradation that exist because of human action.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which form of environmental degradation affects cattle grazers?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Cattle grazers depend on grass and water. When the **desert advances** (desertification), pastures dry up and water points disappear, so herds cannot be fed and herders must move to other areas. Felling of trees and air pollution do not affect grazing as directly, and flooding of river banks affects farmers and settlements near rivers more than it affects grazers.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A programme launched by the Cameroon government to reduce the spread of desertification in the country is...
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Operation Green Sahel** is the government programme of tree planting and soil protection in the northern part of Cameroon, designed to slow down the spread of the desert. The Waza Park Project is about wildlife conservation, the Lagdo dam project is about electricity and water control, and "Green Revolution" refers to agricultural modernisation and not to desertification.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Select the letter below that corresponds to the external administrative units in Cameroon, arranged in descending order.

*Options as printed:* A) Region, Division, Sub-division   B) Division, Sub-division, Region   C) Region, Division, Sub-division   D) Sub-division, Division, Region
questions.corrige_markdown:
The external (field) administrative units of Cameroon, from the largest to the smallest, are the **Region**, then the **Division**, then the **Sub-division**. This order is printed in both options A and C, which have exactly the same wording, so the printed question has two identical correct options and cannot be marked automatically.

**Intended answer: Region, Division, Sub-division (printed identically as A and C).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: Regional Governors have powers to...
questions.corrige_markdown:
A Regional Governor represents the Head of State and the Government in the region and supervises the administration there. Passing a death sentence is a power of the courts, declaring a public holiday belongs to the central authorities and not to a regional authority, and the award of citizenship is handled at the national level. Among the options, the only one that falls within administrative authority exercised at regional level is the recruitment of state employees, so **D** is the answer.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The following are conditions necessary for the creation of administrative units in Cameroon EXCEPT...
questions.corrige_markdown:
An administrative unit is created where it can function properly: the area must be accessible (roads, communication), it must have a large enough population to administer, and it must have enough economic resources to support the administration. The **history and politics of the area** are not conditions for creating an administrative unit.

**Answer: A.**

choix.texte: history and politics of the area.
size of the population of the area.

questions.enonce_markdown: Below are administrative departments which run the services attached to the Presidency of the Republic of Cameroon. Identify the one that ensures the day-to-day running of the Presidency.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The **General Secretariat** of the Presidency is the administrative department that coordinates the services of the Presidency and ensures its daily running. The Civil Cabinet advises the President on matters concerning his office and relations with the public, the High Command is the military authority at the head of the armed forces, and the Presidential Guard ensures the security of the Head of State.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The promotion of the interest of one segment of the population or region of the country above the interest of the entire population describes...
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Sectionalism** is putting the interests of one section (a region, group or part) of the country above the interests of the whole nation. Tribalism is limited to the ethnic or tribal group, favouritism is giving unfair preference to an individual, and bigotry is intolerance of other opinions or groups. The words "one segment of the population or region" match sectionalism best.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which is the BEST definition of nepotism?
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Nepotism** means giving jobs, promotions or other advantages to **members of one's own family** because of the relationship and not because of merit. Option A describes tribalism, option C describes discrimination or ethnic hatred, and option D describes bribery (corruption).

**Answer: B.**

choix.texte: The act of favouring or supporting people from one's village or ethnic group.
The act of giving preferential treatment or favouring one's family members.
The act of showing bias and hatred towards people with different cultures or tribe.
The act of offering something to someone in authority, to gain undeserved favour.

questions.enonce_markdown: The students were disappointed when the Principal appointed his nephew as the school's Senior Prefect, meanwhile many interested candidates were waiting for elections. This Principal is guilty of...
questions.corrige_markdown:
The Principal gave a position to his **nephew**, a member of his family, instead of letting the election decide. Preference for relatives is **nepotism**. Favouritism is a wider word for unfair preference of anyone, tribalism is preference for people of one's tribe, and sectionalism is preference for a region or section, but the case here is clearly about a family relation.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The most common cause of prostitution in Cameroon is...
questions.corrige_markdown:
Many people, especially young girls and women, enter prostitution to earn money when they have no job and no means of support. Although moral education, parental care and peer pressure also matter, **poverty and unemployment** are generally given as the most common cause.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: To fight against the illegal sale of fiscal stamps, the Cameroon Government has introduced the...
questions.corrige_markdown:
Fiscal stamps are used to pay certain taxes and fees on official documents. To prevent forgery and the illegal sale of paper stamps, the Government introduced **franking machines**, which print the stamp value directly on the document at authorised points. Printing stamps abroad, inspecting treasury workers and hand scanners are not the measure that is linked to this problem.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Social reintegration centres in Cameroon are intended to...

*Options as printed:* A) rebuild the character of delinquents.   B) re-educate school drop-outs.   C) restore the dignity of former prostitutes.   D) recover the joy of divorced couples.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Social reintegration (rehabilitation) centres receive young people in difficulty, such as juvenile delinquents, and help them to change their behaviour and return to normal life in society. They can also help other vulnerable persons, so options A and C are both defensible, while B (school drop-outs) belongs to vocational and education services and D (divorced couples) has no link with these centres. The intended answer is to rebuild the character of delinquents.

**Intended answer: A (rebuild the character of delinquents).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: What is national integration?
questions.corrige_markdown:
**National integration** is the process of bringing the different peoples, tribes, languages and cultures of a country together so that they form one nation. Option C expresses this. Option A is limited to politicians, option B describes living in harmony in general, and option D ("one and indivisible") is the principle of national unity and not the definition of integration.

**Answer: C.**

choix.texte: The act of uniting all politicians in Cameroon.
Efforts made by Cameroonians to live in unity and love.
The coming together of all tribes in Cameroon.
The one and indivisibility of Cameroon.

questions.enonce_markdown: Identify the Cameroon National symbol that serves as a sign of honour, dignity and authority.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The **Coat of Arms** is the emblem of the State: it represents the honour, dignity and authority of the Republic and it appears on official documents, buildings and the uniforms of the authorities. The National Flag represents the nation and its unity, the motto "Peace - Work - Fatherland" states the ideals of the country, and the Seal is used to authenticate official documents.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Identify the Constitution that gave birth to the Federal Republic of Cameroon.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The Federal Republic of Cameroon, formed by the union of the former French-administered Cameroon and the former British Southern Cameroons, was established by the **1961 Constitution**. The 1960 Constitution was that of the Republic of Cameroon before the union, the 1972 Constitution replaced the federation with a unitary State, and the 1996 Constitution is a later revision of the unitary State.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The following are provisions of the 1972 Constitution except...
questions.corrige_markdown:
The 1972 Constitution ended the federal system. It created the United Republic of Cameroon, it abolished the federated states and their institutions such as the West Cameroon House of Assembly, and the country was organised into provinces. The fact that **French and English became the official languages** was not a provision of 1972: the two languages were already official under the federal arrangement of 1961.

**Answer: C.**

choix.texte: the United Republic came to existence.
French and English became the official languages.
the West Cameroon House of Assembly was abolished.

questions.enonce_markdown: Identify the three arms of government in Cameroon.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The three arms of government are the **Executive** (which carries out the laws), the **Legislature** (which makes the laws) and the **Judiciary** (which interprets the laws and settles disputes). The Presidency and the Assembly or Parliament are institutions that belong to one of these arms and are not arms themselves.

**Answer: B.**
themes: separation of powers and arms of government

questions.enonce_markdown: Choose the letter which links the two structures that make up the Legislative arm of the government in Cameroon.
questions.corrige_markdown:
In Cameroon the Legislative arm is the Parliament, which is made up of two chambers: the **National Assembly** and the **Senate**. The Court of Impeachment, the Constitutional Council, the Supreme Court and the Supreme State Control (Audit Bench) are other bodies of the State but they are not the two structures of the Legislature.

**Answer: A.**
themes: separation of powers and arms of government

choix.texte: The National Assembly and the Senate
Court of Impeachment and Constitutional Council
Supreme Court and Supreme State Control

questions.enonce_markdown: In which way is the Executive arm of government related to the Judiciary?
questions.corrige_markdown:
In Cameroon the Head of State, who is the head of the Executive, appoints magistrates and takes part in the management of the Judiciary through the Higher Judicial Council. This is a link between the two arms, so **D** is correct. The Judiciary does not control the Executive (A), the Executive does not vote laws, since that is the work of the Legislature (B), and not all members of both arms are appointed (C), since some Executive officials are elected.

**Answer: D.**
themes: separation of powers and arms of government

choix.texte: Members of the Judiciary control members of the Executive
The Executive votes the laws and the Judiciary interprets the laws
Members of the Executive and Judiciary are all appointed
The head of the Executive appoints some members of the Judiciary

questions.enonce_markdown: The electoral code stipulates that to become a member of parliament in Cameroon, a citizen should be able to...
questions.corrige_markdown:
Among the conditions for a candidate to Parliament, the Electoral Code requires the person to know how to read and write and to be able to use an official language (English or French). Option C expresses this. Option A is too strict since it requires both languages, option B is not a legal condition, and option D is not a condition of eligibility.

**Answer: C.**

choix.texte: read and write English and French.
take active part in political rallies.
communicate in any of the official languages.

questions.enonce_markdown: Identify the most important aspect of citizen participation in politics in Cameroon.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The most important and the most widespread form of political participation is **voting**, because it is through the vote that citizens choose their leaders and give them the mandate to govern. Contesting an election, belonging to a party and taking part in a public manifestation are other forms, but they involve fewer people.

**Answer: D.**

choix.texte: Being part of a public manifestation

questions.enonce_markdown: A political party taking part in an election can fight against rigging by...
questions.corrige_markdown:
Rigging happens when results are falsified, most often during counting. A party can prevent this by sending representatives to polling stations to watch and **participate in the counting of votes** and by signing the results. Increasing militants does not stop fraud, publishing registration lists is a task of the electoral body, and boycotting the election removes the party from the process and so does not fight rigging.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: In economic terms, the process of production ends with the...
questions.corrige_markdown:
In economics, production is complete only when goods and services reach the person who uses them. The chain is: raw materials, the manufacturer, the wholesaler, the retailer and finally the **consumer**. The manufacturer, the wholesaler and the retailer are intermediate stages of the chain.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: To which structure are employers of Cameroon obliged to register their workers to enable them benefit from old age pension?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Employers must register their employees with the **National Social Insurance Fund** (CNPS), which collects contributions and pays social benefits such as old age pensions, family allowances and compensation for accidents at work. The National Employment Fund helps people find jobs, and the other two bodies deal with investment and housing.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A situation where there is an increase in gross domestic product accompanied by a corresponding increase in living standards best describes...
questions.corrige_markdown:
Economic growth is only an increase in the gross domestic product (GDP). When this increase comes with better living standards (better health, education, housing and income for the population), we speak of **economic development**. Economic recovery is a return to growth after a fall, and economic decline is a fall in output.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The most important source of government revenue in Cameroon is...
questions.corrige_markdown:
Governments finance public spending mainly from the **taxes** paid by individuals and businesses (direct and indirect taxes, customs duties). Loans and grants are external or occasional resources, and royalties and rents bring in smaller amounts.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: An outstanding effect of tax evasion is...
questions.corrige_markdown:
Tax evasion means refusing to pay, or hiding income to avoid paying, the taxes due. The State then collects less money than it should, so there is a **fall in government revenue** and less money for roads, schools and hospitals. Profiteering, inflation and deflation are not direct effects of tax evasion.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Question 41 is based on the following declaration: "All persons are born free and equal in dignity and rights..." This declaration is from the...
questions.corrige_markdown:
The sentence "All human beings are born free and equal in dignity and rights" is the first article of the **Universal Declaration of Human Rights**, adopted by the United Nations in 1948. The other texts named deal with regional or specific rights and the words of the declaration are those of the Universal Declaration.

**Answer: D.**

choix.texte: International Convention on Civil and Political Rights.
The Universal Declaration of Human Rights.

questions.enonce_markdown: A situation where someone is arrested by security forces, interrogated and forced to say something against his/her wish BEST describes which form of human right violation?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Forcing a person, by pain or pressure, to say something against his or her will during questioning is **torture**. Arbitrary arrest means arresting someone without legal ground, harassment is repeated annoyance or pressure, and human exploitation is making use of a person's work or body for another's profit. The key idea in the question is that the person is forced to speak against his or her will.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The role of the National Commission on Human Rights and Freedoms is to...
questions.corrige_markdown:
The National Commission on Human Rights and Freedoms is a body that promotes and protects human rights. It receives complaints, **investigates** cases of violations and makes reports and recommendations. It does not punish offenders (that is for the courts), it does not give rewards, and it does not pay compensation.

**Answer: D.**

choix.texte: sanction those people who abuse or violate Human Rights.
reward those people who respect Human Rights.
pay damages to victims of Human Rights violations.
investigate incidents and complaints of Human Rights violation.

questions.enonce_markdown: Which institution promotes, guards and implements the International Humanitarian law?
questions.corrige_markdown:
The **International Committee of the Red Cross** (ICRC) is the humanitarian institution that promotes, protects and works for the application of International Humanitarian Law (the Geneva Conventions) by helping victims of war. The International Court of Justice settles disputes between states, the International Criminal Court tries individuals for the gravest crimes, and the WHO deals with health.

**Answer: B.**

choix.texte: The International Committee of the Red Cross

questions.enonce_markdown: All the following are consequences of international conflicts EXCEPT...
questions.corrige_markdown:
International conflicts lead to heavy spending on arms (military expenditure), to bad relations between states (strained relations) and to refugees who flee the fighting. **Frontier violations** (crossing or attacking borders) are more often a cause of conflicts between states than a consequence of them.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Identify the U.N organ that settles disputes and conflicts between states at international level.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The **International Court of Justice**, the principal judicial organ of the United Nations, settles legal disputes between states that agree to bring their cases to it. The General Assembly is a forum for discussion of all member states, the Economic and Social Council deals with economic and social questions, and the Security Council acts mainly to maintain international peace and security.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: In the world of sports, female athletes tend to be paid just a fraction of what their male counterparts earn. This is an example of...
questions.corrige_markdown:
When women and men doing the same work receive very different pay, the two genders are not treated equally: this is **gender inequality**. A stereotype is a fixed belief about how men or women are, bias is an unfair attitude or preference, and violence is physical or psychological harm, none of which is the unequal pay described here.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: They exhibit great cultural talents and are famous for their knowledge of indigenous African medicine. Which minority group best suits this description?
questions.corrige_markdown:
The **Pygmies** (Baka and related groups in the forest areas of the country) are a minority group known for their rich culture of songs and dances and for their knowledge of medicinal plants. The Mbororos are better known as cattle herders, and the Bantus and the Anglophones are not minority groups that fit this description.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: What name is given to the recruitment, transportation and harbouring of children for exploitation?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Recruiting, moving and hiding children in order to exploit them (in work, begging or sexual exploitation) is **child trafficking**. Child labour is making children do work unsuitable for their age, child exploitation is the wider act of using a child for profit, and child abuse is any ill-treatment of a child. The words "recruitment, transportation and harbouring" define trafficking.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The 1951 Convention on Refugees outlines the following solutions to the refugee problem EXCEPT...
questions.corrige_markdown:
The durable solutions to the refugee problem recognised in the refugee protection system are **voluntary repatriation** (return home), **local integration** in the country of asylum and **resettlement** in a third country. The **award of scholarships** is not one of them.

**Answer: A.**
